common_name: Thai Long Green Eggplant (Slender Pale-Green Asian Eggplant)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8–10 weeks before last frost; transplant after all frost danger passes and soil is warm. This slender Southeast Asian type sets fruit reliably through Gulf South summer heat and humidity.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm. Thai Long Green produces slender, curved, pale jade-green fruit up to a foot long with a mild flavor and few seeds, a traditional Southeast Asian type widely used in stir-fries, curries, and grilling, where the thin skin and tender flesh cook quickly without needing to be peeled. The productive, heat-loving plants continue setting fruit through the hottest, most humid stretch of summer, when many Western eggplant varieties slow down. Harvest fruit young and glossy for the best texture — overripe fruit turns dull and develops tougher flesh and larger seeds — and pick every few days to keep plants producing.

planting.note: Start indoors 4–6 weeks before last frost for a spring crop, or in mid to late summer for a fall crop; Romanesco needs a longer, cooler season to head well than standard broccoli.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants generously to give the large outer leaves room to develop. Veronica is an early-maturing, reliable Romanesco selection known for its striking, spiraling, fractal-patterned chartreuse-green heads made up of pointed, pyramidal spirals, a strikingly geometric vegetable with a mild, nutty flavor closer to cauliflower than broccoli. It matures notably faster and more dependably than older Romanesco varieties, an important advantage in regions with a shorter cool season for heading brassicas to develop properly. Harvest the central head while the spirals are still tight before it begins to loosen and flower; in the Gulf South, a fall planting timed to head in cool weather generally outperforms a spring crop, which can bolt as temperatures rise.
